texts.preamble: Da vs Mukhtyar Singh & Ors on 25 April, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 41431/2016 Date of Institution : 01.04.2008 Date of reserving judgement : 25.04.2018 Date of pronouncement : 25.04.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A-1) Sh. Mukhtyar Singh S/o Sh Deedar Singh M/s Chaudhary Sweets, F-4/9, Krishna Nagar, Delhi - 51 R/o B - 13, Krishna Nagar, Delhi -51 A-2) Sh. Deedar Singh M/s Chaudhary Sweets, F-4/9, Krishna Nagar, Delhi - 51 R/o B - 13, Krishna Nagar, Delhi -51 ... Accused person [Proceeding abate vide order dated 17.05.2012] Cc No. 41431/2016 Page No. 1/7 Da vs Mukhtyar Singh & ors Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
texts.facts: As per the complaint, on 29.10.2007 the Food Inspector Ms Usha Kiran purchased a sample of 'Kalakand" a food article for analysis from accused Mukhtyar Singh at M/s Chaudhary Sweets, F-4/9, Krishna Nagar, Delhi - 51, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Mukhtyar Singh was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted 1500 gms of Kalakand (preparation of milk, sugar, pista pieces) taken from open tray without any label declaration. Sample was taken after cutting into smallest pieces of kalakand in a clean and dry steel tray with the help of clean and dry steel knife and mixed properly with the same knife. The sample was divided equally into three clean and dry glass bottles and added 40 dropos of formalin in each bottle. Vendor disclosed that kalakand was prepared from ingredients as mentioned above. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. Kirpa Ram Sharma, SDM/LHA Gandhi Nagar. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Mukhtyar Singh and the price of sample was also given to him DA vs Mukhtyar Singh & ors vide vendor receipt dated 29.10.2007. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No. 1 Mukhtyar Singh and the other witness Sh Mittar Pal, FA. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh Mittar Pal, FA, was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 21/LHA/19542 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated because it contains added starch which is not declared as an ingredient. 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Mukhtyar Singh was the vendor of M/s Chaudhary Sweets, F-4/9, Krishna Nagar, Delhi - 51 at the time of sampling. M/s Chaudhary Sweets is a proprietorship concerned and accused No. 2 Deedar Singh is the proprietor and as such both the vendor and the proprietor are incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. Sample commodity was manufactured by M/s Chaudhary Sweets itslef. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 01.04.2008 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)&(b) of PFA Act, 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. During the trial, the accused No. 2 has expired and proceedings qua DA vs Mukhtyar Singh & ors accused No. 2 were abated vide order dated 17.05.2012. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 01.04.2008. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Da vs Mukhtyar Singh & Ors on 25 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92729904/ 2 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Ms Usha Kiran, PW-2 FI Hukam Singh,, PW3 SDM/LHA Kirpa Ram Sharma and PW-4 FA Mittrapal. PW-1 FI Ms Usha Kiran and PW-4 FA Mittar Pal were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA K.R. Sharma. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Kalakand " 1500 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Kalakand, adding 40 drops of formalin in each sample bottle, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C and raid report Ex.PW1/D. Thereafter one counterpart of sample along with Memo as per Form-VII were deposited to PA for DA vs Mukhtyar Singh & ors analysis vide Ex. PW-1/E and remaining two counter parts along with copies of Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex.PW1/F. Thereafter the PA Report Ex.PW-1/G was received according to which the sample was found adulterated because it contained added starch. Thereafter on the direction of LHA/SDM, PW-1 conducted further the investigation. During investigate PW- 1 sent letter Ex.PW1/H to STO Ward No. 78 and received it reply. Accused Mukhtiar Singh also furnished his statement Ex.PW1/I. Thereafter the case was marked to PW-2 FI Hukum Singh, who put the entire file before the concerned SDM/LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA and obtained the consent for prosecution Ex.PW2/A against the accused persons. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW2/B was filed before the Court and then intimation letter Ex.PW2/C were sent through postal receipt Ex.PW2/D. The Ld Defence Counsel duly cross examined the witness. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 26.09.2014 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter, the accused chose not to lead defence evidence and vide order dated 05.10.2015 defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
